for this workflow, both here and in Donald's original, the model is doing three things.

First, it's generating assets with models and essentially "tracing" over generated references. It's using them to understand motion and sometimes it's just a generative output.

Then it's compositing these into a scene and finally, it's overlaying the typography work and beat matching.

replies.text:
my experience with the Claude family of models is that they do not like using third party software for their workflows. If I make claude use a linear editor with an MCP, it's gonna perform worse than if it uses terminal / browser tools. Three.js vs blender and etc. Not strictly true for everything but if you give a broad direction of "just make a video" or "make a shader" it will do everything in the terminal / browser. 

So while these results may look better for us as viewers, I think the tools are less Claude shaped than pure code. I find opus to be much more clever with its usage when I give no hard constraints other than like, aspect ratio and such. Even a browser shaped tool like remotion which is both something Claude is familiar (react) and browser shaped diminishes the results.

That is not to say it doesn't do well in Blender, it's superior to Fable 5.1 in that regard. But compared to something like Astra, which is eager to do computer use and interact with tools, it's just different. After Effects videos look better out of the box with Astra driving in my brief experience.
